newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraq-based rebels report clash with Iran troops.
newsitem.headline: Iraq-based rebels report clash with Iran troops.

text.p: Iraq-based Iranian rebels said on Wednesday their fighters had killed and wounded a number of government troops in clashes in southeastern Iran.

In a fax sent from its Paris office, the Mujahideen Khalq armed opposition groups said the Tuesday shootout in Zahedan city lasted one hour and a number of troops and security agents were killed and wounded.
There was no independent confirmation of the report which did not give any Mujahideen casualty figures.

The group confirmed an Iranian report on Tuesday about a clash in the central city of Isfahan, but did not refer to Mujahideen casualties. Tehran had said its security forces killed three Mujahideen members and wounded another.
Iran has said its troops killed more than 20 Mujahideen members, who it said had come from neighbouring Iraq to carry out sabotage, in several clashes in the past few weeks.

The Mujahideen have admitted that some of their forces, who they said belonged to underground cells in Iran, were killed. But the group said its fighters had slain or wounded "hundreds" of government troops in a new campaign against the government.
Iran has not reported any casualties among its forces.
Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years.
The Mujahideen have denied attacking civilians, but have taken responsibility for hitting military, government and economic targets.
Iran and Iraq, which fought a war from 1980 to 1988, often accuse each other of backing rebel groups from the other country.
